subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Crystal Growth: Making Pure Silicon
description: A quick win: understand Crystal Growth: Making Pure Silicon.

hook.text: Chip-grade silicon must be 99.999999999% pure. That's eleven nines of purity.

buildup.text: Sand is refined into metallurgical silicon, then converted to a gas for further purification.

discovery.text: The Czochralski process dips a seed crystal into molten silicon and slowly pulls it up.

twist.text: The result is a single crystal ingot up to 300 mm wide — one continuous lattice.

climax.text: Wafers sliced from this ingot become the foundation of billions of chips.

punchline.text: From beach sand to eleven-nines purity — the journey of a silicon wafer.

quiz.question: What is the Czochralski process used for?
options: Etching circuit patterns onto silicon wafers
Growing a single crystal of ultra-pure silicon from a melt
Depositing thin metal layers on semiconductor surfaces
